newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Lover in Cyprus AIDS trial was warned-witness.
newsitem.headline: Lover in Cyprus AIDS trial was warned-witness.

text.p: A British woman who has accused her Cypriot lover of infecting her with the AIDS virus was warned about his condition months before she started sleeping with him, a Cyprus court heard on Friday.

In stark contrast to what 45-year-old AIDS sufferer Janette Pink told the court five weeks ago, Cypriot restaurateur Antonis Kombos, 30, also claimed the woman had another lover when she lived on the holiday island.

Pink, from Basildon, Essex, is charging fisherman Pavlos Georgiou with giving her the HIV virus which leads to Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, accusing him of keeping her in the dark about his condition.
"I had a discussion with Pink and I told her Georgiou had AIDS. She said 'I know, I'm dating him'," Kombos told the court. "I was surprised at how calm she was."
He said that exchange took place in autumn 1993, about three months before Pink and Georgiou started sleeping together.
Pink, a divorcee, has accused Georgiou, 40, of lying to her when he told her his wife was dying of leukaemia. His wife died of AIDS.
Father of four Georgiou, who is HIV positive, has denied the charge.
Pink, who has developed full-blown AIDS and has only a few years left to live, was tested HIV positive in late 1994, nine months after her physical relationship with Georgiou started.
Georgiou, who initially tested positive in 1992, gives no sign of suffering from any illness.

Kombos was brought forward as a character witness for defence at the last minute and said he was testifying of his own volition. "I had a crisis of conscience. In my opinion Pavlos is innocent," he said.
Kombos, who owns a restaurant in the tourist resort of Protaras in south eastern Cyprus, said his acquaintance with Pink dated back to 1988, when she used to visit the island.
He said he used to date Pink's daughter, and Pink was dating a Cypriot called Damianos.
"They slept in the same room. It is hard to believe they didn't have sex," he said.

When she testified in court, Pink had hotly denied suggestions she was dating Damianos and repeatedly accused Georgiou of never telling her his condition and not wearing a condom during intercourse to minimise the risk of infection.
Georgiou claims Pink knew, and that on the one occasion they did have unprotected sex it was because Pink took the condom off him when they were both drunk.
The two sides will sum up the case in court on July 16, while a verdict is expected before courts close for a summer break on August 10.

The outcome of the trial, which has lasted five weeks, could set an important precedent on how to handle allegations of the wilfull or negligent transmission of the killer virus from one person to another.

It is the first case of its kind to reach courts in Cyprus, where the number of HIV carriers and AIDS patients is considered low - around 250 in a population of 650,000. Local statistics show most patients were infected through sexual intercourse.
If found guilty, Georgiou could face a sentence of up to two years in jail or a 1,500 Cyprus pound fine, or both.
